title: Add low-disk check and target/ cleanup; hold jobs when disk is low
summary: Add a minimum-free-disk setting (default 10G) checked before each job and verification; on low space, delete target/ caches of terminal and idle job workspaces, and if still low hold the job as 'environment: low disk' and tell the operator. The audience is the operator running drain. Re-running job 20261016-044847-hem1 (planning pass) is a separate follow-up after this lands, not an edit in this change.

defaults_applied.how: All code and tests are Rust.
New unit and integration tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
The disk minimum is enforced in code before every job and verification, not by prose.
Tests exercise cleanup, hold and resume rather than checking that functions exist.
Docs and comments are written for an outside reader.
One focused change; the hem1 re-run is kept out of the diff.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Re-running hem1 means Athena queues its request again after this lands; the producer does not implement it. The id in the request is 20261016-044847-hem1.
Disk space is read through a small injectable function so tests can simulate low disk without filling the real disk.
Cleanup removes only target/ directories under job workspaces (job dir target/{side}), never sources or records.
A new [disk] section in athena.toml with min_free (default 10G) is parsed in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs; absence of the section means the 10G default.
Held jobs stay queued and are retried in the next drain pass, so verification proceeds once space is freed.
Idle means a workspace of a non-running job untouched for a threshold the producer picks and documents.

acceptance_criteria.text: With free disk simulated below the minimum, a test shows cleanup runs before the job or verification starts. Run `cargo test --locked` and check the new disk tests pass.
A test shows that when space is still low after cleanup, the job is held with the status 'environment: low disk', is not rejected, and the operator is told. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test shows that once space is freed, verification goes ahead for the held job. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test shows a job workspace's target/ is deleted when the job reaches a terminal state, idle workspaces are swept, and source files remain. Run `cargo test --locked`.

athena.toml has a documented minimum-free-disk setting defaulting to 10G, config parsing applies the same default when it is absent, and the docs name the setting and the 'environment: low disk' status.
`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.
The operator can see from the change that a held job is reported in drain output and status with the reason and the free and required amounts.

out_of_scope: Changing the planning-pass code from job hem1 itself in this change
Cleaning anything other than cargo target/ directories
Changing records/ or the verifier's command list
departures: Larger than reference: touches config, drain, state and tests across crates.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed verification attempts: hem1 failed only because the verifier's disk was full, so holding and cleaning avoids redo-work retries.
